title.en: Do I need to see a psychiatrist?

summary.en: Starting from a secondary-school student’s first step in asking for help: when it may be time to seek help, who you can turn to, and how psychiatrists, clinical psychologists, counsellors and occupational therapists differ.
summary.zh: 从一位中学生第一次开口求助的经历说起：什么时候可以考虑寻求帮助、可以找谁，以及精神科医生、临床心理师、辅导员和职能治疗师有什么不同。

title.en: The time of a second glass of water — when a patient’s emotions overflow
title.zh: 第二杯水的时间 – 当病人情绪决堤时

summary.en: A fifteen-year-old breaks down in the consultation room, and the first glass of water doesn’t calm him. Dr. Hanni reflects on why she poured a second one, and on patience and steady presence.
summary.zh: 一位十五岁的少年在诊室里情绪崩溃，第一杯水没能让他平静下来。涵倪医生写下她为什么选择再倒一杯，以及耐心与陪伴的意义。

title.en: “Since my parents died, I thought no one would ever love me again”
title.zh: “自从父母双亡，我以为再也没有人爱我了”

summary.en: Years after her mother’s death, a young woman still can’t make peace with one moment at the bedside. In one conversation she finds a new way to look at it — a note on grief, emotional numbness and facing what we really feel.
summary.zh: 母亲去世多年，她始终放不下临终时的一个画面。一次对话里，她换了个角度重新看待当年的疑问。关于哀伤、情感隔离，以及面对真实的自己。

title.en: If one day you forget who I am
title.zh: 若是有一天，你忘了我是谁

summary.en: An elderly man who brings his wife, recently diagnosed with dementia, to every appointment shares a Hokkien song with Dr. Hanni. A note on companionship, patience and a long marriage.
summary.zh: 一位每次都陪着患失智症的老伴来看诊的老伯伯，分享给涵倪医生一首闽南歌。关于陪伴、耐心，以及老夫老妻之间的珍惜。
